name: Plans lead with problem and solution

pr.title: Lead a plan with the problem and the solution
pr.head: a1e1dcf36e97520a383306eb544079408671ea38

summary: Projector keeps each project's plan in the repository, at docs/projects/<name>/readme.md, with numbered ## N. sections that code and other documents cite. Two things shape a new plan: project create writes a starter file, and the spec skill, skills/spec/SKILL.md, tells an agent what to put in it.

Before this change, the skill asked for an outcome, constraints, acceptance evidence, an implementation sequence, and a list of decisions, and the starter file opened with ## 1. Outcome and ## 2. Acceptance criteria. The design ended up split three ways: the outcome described its effects, each decision held one piece of it, and the implementation sequence described it again as file edits. In the plan that prompted this change, the first line of the design arrived at line 152 of 288, and the reader could not find the fix.

Now a plan leads with what a reviewer needs first. Under the title, one sentence says what the project makes true. Section 1 states the problem for a reader new to the area, and section 2 states the whole solution in one place. The reasons for the design, the acceptance criteria, and, when they have content, cost, rollout, open questions, and background follow in that order. The skill, the starter file, the writing guide, and the two documents that describe plans all change to match.

cards.title: The plan shape this change asks for
cards.html:
PartWhat it holds
SummaryOne sentence under the title: what the project makes true
1. ProblemWhat the system does and why, what goes wrong and how, how much it matters, with one or two pieces of evidence
2. SolutionOne paragraph with the whole fix, then the runtime flow, each data shape as a table, and a table of each file's change
Why this designRationale and rejected alternatives only; repeats none of the solution
Acceptance criteriaObservable evidence that the project is complete
Cost, Rollout, Open questions, BackgroundEach only when it has content; background (logs, counts, code archaeology) comes last

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
Projector reviewed three heads of this pull request. The first review, of ec62b80, opened two findings about how the branch fit the rest of the plan guidance after main renamed the plan-writing skill from design to spec. Both are fixed, and the review of a1e1dcf is clean.

  • The projects README named the design skill. The branch merged main, and bd2df9f names spec.
  • Reshaping an existing plan repurposed cited sections. a1e1dcf keeps each numbered section on its subject and puts the problem and the fix in the unnumbered lead under the title.

The merge of main carries no hand edits, and the validation gate passes on a1e1dcf.

groups.title: The skill asks for the problem, then the solution
groups.kicker: The plan-writing skill's new placement rules and hand-over check
intro: The skill's middle section, which told the agent which parts a plan states and where the three things the review loop checks belong, becomes Lead with the problem, then the solution. It names the first screen a reader sees, the summary, the problem, and the opening paragraph of the solution, and the sections that may follow, in order.

Two smaller rules come with it. A rollout is a numbered sequence only when the steps depend on each other or happen in order across releases; otherwise the solution's file table already says what to change. An existing plan keeps both its section numbers and what each numbered section is about, because other documents cite them; its problem and fix go in the unnumbered lead under the title, and any full new section goes at the end.
The hand-over check at the end of the skill becomes a list, led by whether a reviewer can say what the problem and the fix are after the first screen, and whether the plan describes the design once.

checks.text: Correctness, cost, and reuse, the three things the review loop checks, keep a home: the acceptance criteria, the cost section, and the reasons for the design. The detail the old bullets carried now sits in those section descriptions.

files.note: The placement rules (lines 47 to 127) and the hand-over check (lines 146 to 163) are the substance of the change.

checks.text: A plan from the previous starter file has ## 2. Acceptance criteria. This paragraph keeps § 2 on that subject when the plan is reshaped, so a citation of § 2 still finds the acceptance criteria; the problem and the fix go in the lead above § 1 instead.

groups.title: project create writes the same headings
groups.kicker: The starter plan and the test that pins its headings
intro: ProjectStore.create builds the starter readme.md as one string. It now writes a placeholder summary sentence under the title and four numbered sections: Problem, Solution, Why this design, and Acceptance criteria. The optional sections are left out, because the skill adds each only when it has content.
A new test creates a plan and checks the exact headings, their order, the summary placeholder, and that the old Outcome heading is gone.

files.note: Only the scaffold string changes; the frontmatter and the exclusive create around it are untouched.

checks.text: Ran project create and a nested project create --parent from this head in a scratch repository: both plans carry the summary placeholder and the four headings in order, and project check prints Project plans are valid.
The full suite passes on this head: 443 tests, OK (skipped=1). The skip is the compiled-script check, which needs npm ci.

groups.title: The guides describe the same shape
groups.kicker: The projects README, the CLI reference, and the writing guide
intro: Three documents describe plans, and each now matches the skill. docs/projects/README.md is the convention every adopting repository reads before it changes a plan; its Write a project plan section now spells out the shape. docs/cli.md says what project create writes. The writing guide's § 3 sorts each part of a plan by the job it does, and now says the problem and the solution describe the system while the reasons explain it.

files.note: The new paragraph describes the shape and says the spec skill fills the scaffold.
One added sentence on what the starter plan contains, matching core.py.
Replaces the sentence that called the implementation sequence a how-to and the decisions an explanation.
